aiEstimate.basis: Strict proof-completion estimate: 0%. Exact identities and local descent cases are proved, but no argument establishes descent for every starting integer. Finite coverage does not give a meaningful percentage of the full theorem.

focus.status: Pure-math strategy · global descent theorem open
focus.title: Derive an orbit-wide bound from block dynamics
focus.summary: At the sole possible mean-test gap, a genuine expansion has two exact branches: either the next run is shorter and a_next+t_next≤a_k−1, or the run grows while u is preserved and the following block is also forced to expand. Neutral equality is a periodic return. The global task remains an all-starting-values bound from the coupled transitions.
focus.next: Prove a structural lower bound on Σ(a_k−1) from the transition law and compare it with the non-descent cap.

accomplishments.title: Proof target made precise
accomplishments.detail: Reduce the full conjecture to showing that every odd n > 1 has a smaller odd iterate under the Syracuse map.

accomplishments.title: Exact cumulative-valuation criterion derived
accomplishments.detail: For an odd Syracuse orbit, 2^A_j S^j(n) = 3^j n + c_j and descent is equivalent to (2^A_j − 3^j)n > c_j.

accomplishments.title: Exact run length of valuation-one steps proved
accomplishments.detail: Starting from odd n, exactly v2(n+1)−1 consecutive Syracuse steps have valuation 1; the following step has valuation at least 2. This proves larger valuations recur, but not often enough yet to force descent.

accomplishments.title: Exact return-block descent criterion derived
accomplishments.detail: For a valuation-a≥2 step followed by its forced run of t−1 valuation-one steps, the endpoint satisfies 3(z−x)=2^a−2−u(2^{a+t}−2·3^t). This gives an exact local test, while allowing some blocks to grow.

accomplishments.title: Modulo-three restriction on return blocks proved
accomplishments.detail: The block integrality equation forces 3|u for odd a, and u≡(−1)^{t+1} mod 3 for even a. This raises the minimum possible u and sharpens sufficient local descent conditions.

accomplishments.title: Exact transition law between return blocks derived
accomplishments.detail: Successive blocks satisfy a_{k+1}−1=v2(3^{t_k}u_k−1), equivalently 3^{t_k}u_k−1=2^{a_{k+1}−1}(2^{t_{k+1}}u_{k+1}−1). The long-run consequence is still open.

accomplishments.title: Critical mean for local block descent proved
accomplishments.detail: If a block's mean valuation (a+t−1)/t is at most log₂3, its endpoint is strictly larger than its start. Therefore a contracting block must exceed this mean, but that condition alone is not sufficient.

accomplishments.title: Guaranteed-descent mean threshold derived
accomplishments.detail: A block is guaranteed to contract when q=(a+t−1)/t exceeds λ_t=1+(1/t)log₂((3^t−1)/(2^t−1))=log₂3+η_t, with η_t positive and tending to zero. The coarse test is inconclusive in the band between thresholds.

accomplishments.title: Explicit bound on the threshold gap derived
accomplishments.detail: Writing η_t=(1/t)log₂(1+δ_t), where δ_t=(2^{-t}−3^{-t})/(1−2^{-t}), gives 0<η_t<2^{1−t}/(t ln 2). The local uncertainty shrinks exponentially with block length.

accomplishments.title: Exact logarithmic block-drift identity derived
accomplishments.detail: The endpoint ratio telescopes to Σ(a_k−1)=j log₂(3/2)+Σε_k−log₂((x_{m+1}+1)/(n+1)), where each ε_k is positive and bounded by −log₂(1−2^{-t_k}). This gives a block-length-sensitive necessary cap, not a proof of descent.

accomplishments.title: Exact state-dependent block contraction test derived
accomplishments.detail: A block contracts exactly when q_k exceeds log₂3 plus ε_k/t_k, where ε_k=log₂(1+(2^{a_k}−2)/(3(x_k+1))). Summed block drift below −r log₂(3/2) places a block-boundary iterate below the original n.

accomplishments.title: Cumulative block-excess constraint derived
accomplishments.detail: Across m complete blocks, A_j−j=Σ(a_k−1). If the orbit never drops below n, this excess must be at most j log₂((3+1/n)/2) at each block boundary. Proving a contradictory lower bound remains open.

accomplishments.title: Monotone block threshold proved
accomplishments.detail: The universal sufficient mean λ_t=log₂3+η_t decreases strictly to log₂3. Thus any fixed margin above log₂3 guarantees contraction for sufficiently long blocks; whether every orbit attains the needed means remains open.

accomplishments.title: Mean tests isolate one possible valuation gap
accomplishments.detail: For fixed block length t, a≤floor(t log₂(3/2))+1 forces expansion, while a≥floor(t log₂(3/2))+3 guarantees contraction. At most one integer a remains for the exact u-dependent test; this is local and does not control orbit-wide drift.

accomplishments.title: The possible valuation gap reduced to an integer test
accomplishments.detail: For the sole candidate a=floor(t log₂(3/2))+2, universal contraction is immediate if 1−{t log₂(3/2)}>log₂R_t. Otherwise the exact block test is uD>2^{h+1}−1, where h=floor(t log₂(3/2)) and D=2^{h+t+1}−3^t>0. This remains a local criterion.

accomplishments.title: An expanding gap block forces the next valuation down
accomplishments.detail: For a=h+2 and uD≤2^{h+1}−1, the transition law gives a_next−1=v₂(Du+1). Strict expansion implies a_next≤a−1; equality in the block test is a periodic return. This is a local transition constraint, not a global descent proof.

accomplishments.title: Expanding gap blocks split into two exact transitions
accomplishments.detail: For a strict expansion, write r=Du+1=2^b s with s odd and ℓ=t+h+1−b. If s>1, then a_next+t_next≤a_k−1; if s=1, then t_next=ℓ≥t+1 and u_next=u. This is an exact local dichotomy, not a global descent proof.

accomplishments.title: The long-run branch forces a second expansion
accomplishments.detail: In the s=1 branch after a strict gap-block expansion, t_next≥t+1, u_next=u, and q_next=1+b/t_next<log₂3. The critical mean test therefore forces the next block to expand too. This is still only a local sequence constraint.

notes.speaker: Project direction
notes.text: The project is pivoting from the UCT conjecture to Collatz. The plan is to move slowly, use small checkable tasks, and build a map toward a full proof.

notes.speaker: Codex · research update
notes.text: Earlier, we proved a local descent certificate for n ≡ 2587 (mod 4096). It remains a partial result; the current direction studies general valuation identities.

notes.speaker: Codex · theory update
notes.text: We grouped the orbit into blocks: each has length t and valuation sum a+t−1, so A_j−j=Σ(a_k−1). A non-descending orbit must keep this excess below j log₂((3+1/n)/2) at block boundaries. The missing step is a dynamics-based lower bound; blocks can expand, as 9→7→11→17 shows.

notes.speaker: Codex · algebra update
notes.text: Using 3x=2^{a+t}u−2^a−1, integrality forces u to be divisible by 3 when a is odd, and fixes u modulo 3 when a is even. This sharpens which return blocks can contract; the global cumulative bound is still open.

notes.speaker: Codex · dynamics update
notes.text: A block contracts exactly when q_k>log₂3+ε_k/t_k. Summed block drifts below −r log₂(3/2) guarantee a return value below n. The open task is an orbit-wide inequality forcing such descent for every odd start.

notes.speaker: Project direction
notes.text: The proof path is centered on exact Syracuse identities, valuation constraints, and inequalities that apply to every odd starting value. Finite orbit checks and growing residue tables are kept outside the proof strategy.

notes.speaker: Codex · threshold update
notes.text: The universal block threshold λ_t decreases strictly to log₂3. Any fixed positive margin above log₂3 therefore guarantees contraction for sufficiently long blocks. Proving that the coupled parameters of every orbit supply this margin remains open.

notes.speaker: Codex · local criterion update
notes.text: For each fixed block length t, the mean tests classify every valuation a except possibly one integer level: lower a forces expansion, higher a guarantees contraction, and the single possible gap is resolved by the exact u-dependent formula. This narrows a local criterion only; the global orbit problem remains open.

notes.speaker: Codex · arithmetic refinement
notes.text: The one possible valuation gap now has an exact integer form. For h=floor(t log₂(3/2)) and a=h+2, the block contracts exactly when u(2^{h+t+1}−3^t)>2^{h+1}−1. The open challenge is to control these u values across the coupled orbit.

notes.speaker: Codex · transition update
notes.text: At the sole possible mean-test gap, put M=2^{h+1} and D=2^{h+t+1}−3^t. If uD<M−1, the block expands but the exact transition gives a_next−1=v₂(Du+1)≤h, so the next high valuation is at least one smaller. Equality uD=M−1 returns to the same block start and is periodic. This does not settle the global orbit.

notes.speaker: Codex · transition refinement
notes.text: A strict expansion at the exceptional valuation has two exact next-block forms. With r=Du+1=2^b s and ℓ=t+h+1−b: s>1 forces a_next+t_next≤a_k−1; s=1 gives t_next=ℓ≥t+1 and preserves u_next=u. This narrows the local recurrence but leaves global orbit control open.

notes.speaker: Codex · next-block update
notes.text: The s=1 branch has a further consequence: b≤h≤t log₂(3/2), while t_next=ℓ≥t+1, so q_next=1+b/ℓ<log₂3. Hence the following block is forced to expand too. In the s>1 branch, t_next<t and a_next+t_next≤a_k−1. No global descent follows yet.
